longForm.overview:

Where ⬛ reads as solid-black-coded trans-symbol read and ⬜ reads as solid-white-coded trans-symbol read, ⚧ captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate gender coded trans-symbol — a 'gender ⚧' gender-marker marker or a 'gender-pulse pulse ⚧' gender-marker reveal. The gender fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern gender-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as gender coded rather than literal trans-symbol-coded shape.

In real-world usage ⚧ lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate gender-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'gender ⚧' gender-marker marker. A friend sends it on a 'gender-pulse pulse ⚧' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'gender coded ⚧' list thread. The gender fill cue is what makes the emoji feel gender coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'gender coded trans-symbol moment.'

What separates ⚧ from the rest of the shape family is the gender register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'gender coded trans-symbol,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition. That is why ⚧ travels especially well on partner gender-marker markers, gender-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with gender energy.
